name: Notary server
description: The TUF-based signing service Docker Content Trust talks to. Stores signed metadata (root.json, snapshot.json, timestamp.json, targets.json) for image-tag → digest mappings. Configurable via `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST_SERVER` (default `https://notary.docker.io` for Docker Hub).

name: Notary signer
description: The notary component that holds the snapshot+timestamp signing keys server-side (so they can rotate automatically without dropping clients). Distinct from the user-controlled root/targets keys.

name: TUF repository
description: The Update Framework metadata layout DCT uses: a hierarchy of signed JSON files (root → targets → delegations → snapshot → timestamp) that together attest a specific image-tag → digest binding. Industry-standard, designed to survive a partial key compromise.

name: dockerd TLS listener
description: The mTLS-secured TCP socket dockerd opens when configured with `--tlsverify` + cert pair. Default port 2376 (vs 2375 for unencrypted). Mandatory in modern Docker — daemon refuses to start with a plain TCP listener.

name: rootless userland runtime
description: The dockerd-rootless wrapper (`dockerd-rootless-setuptool.sh`) that launches dockerd inside a user namespace using `newuidmap` / `newgidmap`. Runs as user-mode systemd service under `~/.config/systemd/user/docker.service`. Uses `slirp4netns` (or `vpnkit` on Mac) for unprivileged networking.

name: AppArmor profile
description: LSM profile loaded into the kernel via `apparmor_parser`. Docker auto-loads `docker-default` and applies it per container; override with `--security-opt apparmor=<name>`. Profile DSL: capabilities, file rules, network rules, mount/ptrace/signal/dbus access. Ubuntu/Debian default; SUSE optional.

name: seccomp profile (security view)
description: JSON-format syscall filter loaded into the kernel via the `seccomp()` syscall. Docker's default profile (moby/profiles/seccomp/default.json) blocks ~44 of 300+ syscalls. Allowlist semantics: defaultAction `SCMP_ACT_ERRNO` (deny+EPERM); per-syscall overrides to `SCMP_ACT_ALLOW`. CONFIG_SECCOMP=y kernel + Docker built with seccomp required.

name: SELinux context
description: Type-enforcement label on processes and files. Format `user:role:type:level`. Docker assigns `container_t` to container processes by default on SELinux-enabled hosts; bind mounts get `container_file_t`. `:z` / `:Z` on a `-v` mount relabels the host path.

name: capability bounding set
description: Per-process kernel limit on which capabilities a process and its descendants can ever hold. Docker default-drops most caps, leaving only: chown, dac_override, fowner, fsetid, kill, setgid, setuid, setpcap, net_bind_service, net_raw, sys_chroot, mknod, audit_write, setfcap. Override via `--cap-add` / `--cap-drop`.

name: UID mapping (security view)
description: User-namespace mapping `containerID hostID size` written to `/proc/<pid>/uid_map`. Container root (uid 0) → some non-zero host uid (e.g. 165536). Without CAP_SETUID, only `newuidmap` SETUID binary can write multi-range mappings (consults /etc/subuid).

name: GID mapping (security view)
description: Same pattern for groups via `/proc/<pid>/gid_map` and `newgidmap`.

name: /etc/subuid
description: Per-user subordinate UID range allocations. Format `username:start:count` per line. Required for userns-remap mode (`dockremap` user) and rootless mode. Need ≥ 65,536 subordinate UIDs.

name: /etc/subgid
description: Same as subuid for GID ranges. `usermod --add-subuids/--add-subgids` or manual edits.

name: slirp4netns
description: Userspace TCP/IP stack (TUN-based) used by rootless dockerd to give containers network access without CAP_NET_ADMIN. Slower than kernel-bridge networking; `--rootless` containers route through it. Configurable via `DOCKERD_ROOTLESS_ROOTLESSKIT_NET=slirp4netns`.

name: vpnkit
description: Mac-equivalent of slirp4netns used by Docker Desktop. User-space VPN+TUN that forwards container traffic from the Linux VM to the host.

name: userns-remap mode
description: Daemon-level user-namespace remapping. Configured via daemon.json `userns-remap: "default"` (uses `dockremap` system user) or `userns-remap: "<user>:<group>"`. Container root (uid 0) maps to host's non-zero uid. Mutually exclusive with `--privileged`, `--ipc=host`, `--net=host`, `--pid=host` containers. Bind-mount/volume ownership becomes the remapped uid — common foot-gun.

name: rootless mode
description: Run the daemon AND containers WITHOUT root privileges. Distinct from userns-remap, where dockerd is root but containers are remapped. Rootless = dockerd as a normal user inside its own user namespace. Limits: cgroup v1 doesn't support cgroup-delegation in rootless; AppArmor not supported on Debian-derived; checkpoint/restore unsupported; no overlay2 on kernels < 5.13 (uses fuse-overlayfs).

name: Docker Content Trust (DCT)
description: Image signing via TUF. Set `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1` in the env to enable; affected commands: `pull`, `push`, `build`, `create`, `run`. With DCT on, pulls reject unsigned images; pushes auto-sign. Tag-to-digest binding becomes immutable.

name: mTLS daemon socket
description: Mutual-TLS on dockerd's TCP listener. Daemon: `--tlsverify --tlscacert=ca.pem --tlscert=server.pem --tlskey=server-key.pem -H tcp://0.0.0.0:2376`. Client picks via `DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY=1` + `DOCKER_CERT_PATH=…`. Mandatory for any production TCP exposure — daemon refuses non-TLS TCP listeners.

name: default seccomp profile
description: `moby/profiles/seccomp/default.json` is auto-applied to every container. Blocks ~44 syscalls (acct, add_key, bpf, clock_settime, create_module, init_module, kexec_*, keyctl, mount, ptrace under restrictive caps, reboot, swap*, sysctl, umount, unshare, …). Disable with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined`; replace with `--security-opt seccomp=<file>`.

name: default AppArmor profile
description: `docker-default` profile loaded by dockerd at startup on AppArmor-enabled hosts. Generated programmatically; can be regenerated and tweaked. Per-container override: `--security-opt apparmor=<name>` or `apparmor=unconfined`.

name: no-new-privileges
description: Sets `no_new_privs` bit on the container's pid 1. Prevents setuid binaries from gaining new caps via execve. Enable per-container with `--security-opt no-new-privileges:true`; daemon-wide via daemon.json `no-new-privileges: true`. Cheap, strong baseline hardening.

name: read-only rootfs
description: `docker run --read-only` mounts container root as RO. Combine with explicit `--tmpfs /tmp` for writable scratch space. Stops attackers from persisting payloads in the container's writable layer.

name: tmpfs noexec
description: Default tmpfs flags Docker applies: `rw,noexec,nosuid,size=65536k`. The `noexec` is the security-relevant bit — prevents executing dropped binaries from /dev/shm or /tmp.

name: cap-drop=ALL baseline
description: Hardening pattern: `--cap-drop=ALL` then selective `--cap-add=NET_BIND_SERVICE` (etc.). The least-privilege baseline. Combined with `--security-opt no-new-privileges:true` and `--read-only`, gives a strong minimal-privilege container.

name: SELinux enforcement
description: Daemon-level `selinux-enabled: true` enables container_t labeling. Containers are then confined by the SELinux policy (RHEL/CentOS/Fedora). Bind mount `:z` (shared label) / `:Z` (private label) modifies the host label. WARNING: bind-mounting system dirs with `:Z` can render the host inoperable.

name: image signing (cosign / sigstore)
description: Modern alternative to DCT/Notary: keyless OIDC-based signatures (cosign) attached as referrers to the image manifest in OCI registries. Verified via `cosign verify`. Replaces TUF-based DCT for many supply-chain teams.

name: TUF root key
description: Top-level offline-stored signing key. Signs `root.json` (the trust anchor). Compromise = full takeover; rotation requires offline ceremony. Generated with `docker trust key generate`. Format: encrypted PEM under `~/.docker/trust/private/<sha256>.key`.

name: TUF repository key (targets-of-targets)
description: Per-image-repository signing key (a.k.a. tagging key). Created on first push of a repo with DCT enabled. Signs `targets/releases.json`. Held by repo maintainers.

name: TUF targets key
description: Top-level targets key — controls which delegations/keys are trusted to sign tags. Held offline alongside root.

name: TUF snapshot key
description: Signs `snapshot.json` — the consistent hash of all metadata at a point in time. By default held by Notary server (so it can rotate frequently); can be moved client-side for stricter posture.

name: TUF timestamp key
description: Signs `timestamp.json` — short-lived signature attesting freshness. Always held server-side (must rotate continuously). Defends against replay attacks.

name: TUF delegation key
description: Per-delegated-role signing key (e.g. `targets/<delegation>`). Lets repo owners scope signing capability to subsets of tags or specific signers. Useful for CI signing limited tag ranges.

name: DCT passphrase
description: Per-key passphrase encrypting the on-disk PEM. Env vars to supply non-interactively: `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST_REPOSITORY_PASSPHRASE`, `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST_OFFLINE_PASSPHRASE`, `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST_TARGETS_PASSPHRASE`. Required for CI signing.

name: cosign keypair
description: `cosign generate-key-pair` produces `cosign.key` (encrypted) and `cosign.pub`. Signature attached as a referrer manifest to the image. Or keyless: OIDC token from a CI provider (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) signs ephemerally — Fulcio mints a short-lived cert.

name: defense in depth
description: Layered hardening: namespaces (isolation) + cgroups (resource limits) + capabilities (privilege fragmentation) + seccomp (syscall filter) + AppArmor/SELinux (LSM) + read-only rootfs + no-new-privileges + signed images. Each layer only has to slow an attacker down; together they make container escape very expensive.

name: least privilege
description: Drop everything by default; add only what the workload needs. `--cap-drop=ALL` + selective `--cap-add` is the canonical knob. Same idea applies to volumes (read-only), network (--network=none unless needed), and seccomp (custom profile blocking unused syscalls).

name: daemon-socket attack surface
description: `docker.sock` is root-equivalent for whoever can write to it. Mounting `/var/run/docker.sock` into a container = handing the container root on the host. Common foot-gun in 'CI runner' containers. Mitigation: use a docker-in-docker setup with strict TLS, OR use an authorization plugin to gate the API.

name: image supply chain
description: The full path from source code to running container: source repo → CI build → base-image source → registry → puller → runtime. Each hop is an attack surface. DCT / cosign sign each hop's output; provenance attestations document the build environment; SBOM lists ingredients.

name: kernel vulnerability exposure
description: Containers share the host kernel — a kernel CVE that lets a privileged-enough syscall escape namespace = container escape. Default seccomp blocks the worst offenders (kexec_*, init_module, perf_event_open, …). Defense: keep kernel patched, run with seccomp on, drop CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

name: container escape
description: A class of vulns where a process inside a container gains code execution outside it. Vectors: kernel CVE + permissive seccomp; CAP_SYS_ADMIN + setns; mounting host-fs paths inside a privileged container; runc CVEs. Each class is mitigated by a different layer of defense-in-depth.

name: cgroup v2 vs v1 security
description: v2 unified hierarchy supports cgroup-delegation (an unprivileged user can manage their own subtree). v1's per-controller hierarchies don't — rootless dockerd needs v2 for full functionality. Per docker docs, 'Cgroup delegation is not secure in cgroups v1.'

name: CRI vs docker-engine attack surface
description: On k8s nodes since 1.24, kubelet talks to containerd via CRI directly (no dockerd). Removes the docker.sock attack surface entirely. Trade-off: lose `docker` CLI on the node — `crictl` is the equivalent. Important context for Kubernetes hardening.

name: TLS certificate pinning
description: Trusting only a specific CA cert (or even leaf cert) for the daemon socket. Defends against rogue CAs. Configured via `--tlscacert` on both daemon and client. With `tlsverify` on, anything not chained to the pinned CA is rejected.

name: certificate rotation
description: Daemon TLS certs rotate via daemon restart with a new key/cert pair (graceful rotation requires brief overlap). Notary timestamp/snapshot keys rotate automatically server-side. Long-lived offline root keys are the rotation pain point.

name: signed image pull
description: With `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1`, `docker pull <repo>:<tag>` resolves the tag through Notary instead of trusting the registry's tag-to-digest mapping. Rejects pulls of unsigned tags. The user-facing piece of DCT.

name: unprivileged user namespaces
description: Kernel feature that lets non-root users create user namespaces. Required by rootless mode. Some distros disable it (`/proc/sys/kernel/unprivileged_userns_clone=0`); enable with `sysctl -w kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1` (Debian) or `user.max_user_namespaces` tuning.

name: cgroup delegation (systemd)
description: systemd's `Delegate=yes` on a user-mode service lets it own its cgroup subtree. Required for rootless dockerd to enforce per-container resource limits. v2 unified-hierarchy only.

name: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR
description: Per-user runtime dir (`/run/user/<uid>`). Rootless dockerd uses it for sockets, pid files, etc. Must be writable by the user; cleaned at logout. Persistent rootless services need `loginctl enable-linger <user>` so the dir survives logout.

name: path-traversal via volume mount
description: Class of attack where a malicious image / Dockerfile mounts `/` (or `/etc`, `/var/lib`) from the host and reads/writes outside the container's intended scope. Mitigation: never run untrusted images with `--privileged`, audit `-v` / `--mount` carefully, use userns-remap so container writes aren't host root.
